newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore rubber ends easier on liquidation.
newsitem.headline: Singapore rubber ends easier on liquidation.

text.p: Rubber futures closed marginally easier on Wednesday on the back of liquidation by market players, especially for RSS3 grade rubber, dealers said.
"We ran into some modest liquidation by local dealers trying to cover their positions. But the volume in the other rubber brands was relatively slim," a dealer for a rubber trading house said.
Firmer prices in Tokyo, where its benchmark August contract rose 2.3 yen to settle at 156.3, helped to shore up market sentiment, dealers said.

The volume traded of RSS3 rubber for spot April shipment reached around 2,000 tonnes. The total traded for RSS1 rubber reached about 800 tonnes while TSR20 rubber volume was a meagre 300 tonnes, dealers said.
At around 0945 GMT, April RSS3 was seen at 120.50-122.50 U.S. cents a kg from the previous 122.50 cents.
April RSS1 was seen at 172.50-174.50 Singapore cents (US$1.20-$1.22) a kg from 174.50 cents.
May TSR20 was seen at 167.50-169.50 Singapore cents (US$1.17-$1.18) a kg from the previous 169.50 cents.
